official_lima_claim.museum_label: Daga egipcia de bronce del faraon Tutmosis III 1200 AC
official_lima_claim.mincetur_description: bronze-and-wood Egyptian dagger bearing the personal emblem of Pharaoh Thutmose III

epigraphy.reading_A_legacy: Mn-kheper-Re-user / Mn-ḫpr-Rʿ-wsr, attributed by the legacy Global Egyptian Museum record to Thutmose III
epigraphy.reading_B_pietri_2016: Mn-kheperu-Re-user / Mn-ḫpr.w-Rʿ-wsr, read by Renaud Pietri from photography as an otherwise unattested-looking variant of Mn-kheperu-Re, the throne name of Thutmose IV
epigraphy.independent_scholarly_support: A warfare/weapon study also describes Florence inv. 7677 as having a plain wooden grip incised with the throne name of Thutmose IV.
epigraphy.plain_language_verdict: The inscription belongs to the Menkheperre/Menkheperure royal-name family. The present public evidence does not justify a fixed translation or a confident Thutmose III attribution for the photographed dagger. Thutmose IV is a serious published alternative.

florence_identity_comparator.inventory: Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Firenze inv. 7677
florence_identity_comparator.reported_acquisition: reputedly bought in Luxor by Ernesto Schiaparelli in 1891-1892
diagnostic_features: blade shoulders incompletely covered by grip
two strongly stylized opposing falcon heads at pommel
possible_explanations: older blade mounted with later handle

lima_vs_florence.reason: The official Lima photograph visibly shows the same rare diagnostic class emphasized in scholarship for Florence inv. 7677, especially the opposing falcon-head pommel, composite wood/metal construction, riveted join and royal-name marking.
lima_vs_florence.prohibited_claim: Do not assert that the Lima and Florence photographs show the same physical object until high-resolution landmark comparison and museum confirmation are obtained.
required_confirmation: museum confirmation that website photograph is of their physical holding
Florence inv. 7677 current catalogue images and measurements

chronology_control.result: 1200 BCE label does not by itself disprove a Thutmose III-associated royal name
chronology_control.reason: Metropolitan Museum records show Menkheperre, Thutmose III's throne name, continued on objects long after his reign, including Ramesside and later contexts.
chronology_control.implication: Date, name, manufacture, reuse and posthumous cult must be separated.

critical_1956_locator.decision_rule: If the dagger is documented in the 1956 catalogue, presence in Mujica Gallo's collection by 1956 is strongly anchored; if absent, prioritize later auction/travel/acquisition records.

osiris_firewall.usefulness: The Lima dagger is a provenance-method and collection-dispersal control. It can join the Osiris/CROFT mainline only if a source-bound acquisition/dealer/custody node intersects known Mendes dispersal documentation.

required_inputs: Florence inv. 7677 current record and image confirmation
